set_aside.subject: revocation observed by an in-flight request
set_aside.text: “Immediate” revocation is changed to “every request authenticated after the revocation commits observes it”, while INV-005 and M07 still say revocation blocks “the next authorization check immediately”.
set_aside.question: If a request authenticates before revocation commits but reaches its project-scope or capability check afterward, must authorization_guard reject it?
options: Reject it because every authorization check reads current revocation state.
Allow it because only requests authenticated after the commit are required to observe revocation.
set_aside.default_guess: Reject it at the post-commit authorization check.

witness.initial: An operator has an active session and active assignment to project P.
events: An administrator revokes the assignment and commits.
The original request then reaches its project authorization check.
outcomes: The request is rejected because the next authorization check observes the revoked assignment.
The request proceeds because it authenticated before the revocation committed.
witness.observer: The operator and anyone observing whether the project operation changes or returns data.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: implicit manual-budget creation during progress read
set_aside.text: “project_tracking.list_project_progress creates the empty manual budget version” conflicts with State 3 assigning the manual budget to budget_management and saying that the use case owning an operation opens and closes its transaction; the texts do not say which module owns this write, its audit occurrence, or the transaction spanning the read and write.
set_aside.question: Does project_tracking own the implicit budget creation inside the progress-read transaction, or does it invoke a separately transactional budget_management operation, and which module builds the required budget.manual_version_create audit record?
options: project_tracking performs the creation and audit in the same transaction as list_project_progress.
budget_management performs and audits creation in its own transaction before project_tracking reads progress.
budget_management supplies non-transactional creation logic that project_tracking invokes inside project_tracking's transaction.
set_aside.default_guess: Have budget_management supply the budget mechanism while project_tracking owns one transaction and the audit for this progress-read-triggered occurrence.

witness.initial: Project P is archived and has no manual BudgetVersion.
events: An authorized staff member requests P's progress list.
The empty manual budget is created as required.
A later progress-row read fails with a persistence error before the response is produced.
outcomes: Creation and its audit roll back with the failed progress read, so P still has no manual budget.
A separately committed budget-management operation leaves the empty budget and audit persisted although the progress request fails.
witness.observer: The staff member on a retry and an administrator reading the audit or budget history.

set_aside.subject: identification of the viewer sign-out route
set_aside.text: transport_guard “checks the origin of viewer sign-out” and must do so before routing, but its Knows section names only models; the sign-out endpoint is owned by api_irregular and no canonical sign-out path or route marker is owned by a module transport_guard may know.
set_aside.question: From which owned fact does transport_guard determine that a request is viewer sign-out?
options: transport_guard owns a duplicated literal sign-out path.
api or api_irregular exports route identity that is supplied to transport_guard during composition.
runtime supplies a shared route predicate or marker whose owner is explicitly named.
set_aside.default_guess: Supply the route identity from the API composition rather than duplicate the path in transport_guard.

witness.initial: The viewer API exposes a sign-out endpoint, but State 3 gives no concrete path to transport_guard.
events: One implementer chooses /viewer/logout as the guarded path.
A foreign-origin browser submits the actual sign-out request.
outcomes: The request is recognized as sign-out and rejected before the handler.
The guard does not recognize the route, so the foreign-origin sign-out reaches the handler.
witness.observer: The viewer whose session is or is not terminated.
